{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"c07e983786404f166255735ed7d69926369ef7526a36b33b5adeb29c9707dafe","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:82","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Revocation and suspension grounds, vehicle impound, violation points and Traffic Survival School, chemical test refusal, financial responsibility, failure to appear and traffic ticket enforcement","heading":"C — Offenses that bring revocation or suspension, when a vehicle is impounded, how violation points add up to Traffic Survival School, the reasons MVD may act on a license, chemical test refusal, driving on a suspended license, insurance violations, and missed court dates and unpaid fines","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Offenses that bring revocation or suspension, when a vehicle is impounded, how violation points add up to Traffic Survival School, the reasons MVD may act on a license, chemical test refusal, driving on a suspended license, insurance violations, and missed court dates and unpaid fines
Knowledge domain: which offenses lead to revocation and which to suspension, when police must impound or immobilize a vehicle, how many points each violation adds and when points require Traffic Survival School (TSS), the reasons MVD may suspend, revoke or require TSS, the chemical test refusal penalty, the penalties for driving while suspended and for lacking proof of insurance, and what happens when you miss court or leave fines unpaid.

FACT_ID: sec19-F01 | anchor: A01
Any homicide or aggravated assault involving the use of a vehicle leads to revocation of your driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F02 | anchor: A01
Any felony committed with the use of a vehicle leads to revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F03 | anchor: A01
Lying under oath about who owns or operates a vehicle leads to revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F04 | anchor: A01
Failing to stop and give aid at the scene of a traffic crash you are involved in leads to revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F05 | anchor: A01
Having two or more DUI convictions leads to revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F06 | anchor: A01
An aggravated DUI conviction leads to revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F07 | anchor: A01
Causing a death or serious physical injury by using a vehicle leads to revocation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F08 | anchor: A01
Two or more convictions for reckless driving, or two or more for racing on the highways, lead to suspension of your driving privilege. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F09 | anchor: A01
Your privilege may also be revoked if you do not take and pass a driving retest that you were required to take. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F10 | anchor: A01
Your privilege may be revoked if you are found medically, psychologically or physically unable to operate a motor vehicle. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F11 | anchor: A01
Your privilege may be revoked if your continued driving would endanger public health, safety or welfare. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F12 | anchor: A01
A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when the driver's privilege is suspended or revoked for any reason. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F13 | anchor: A01
A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when the driver has never held a valid license or permit and cannot show an out-of-state license. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F14 | anchor: A01
A vehicle must be impounded or immobilized when a driver who must use an ignition interlock device is driving without a working certified device. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F15 | anchor: A01
Suspension is the temporary removal of your driving privilege, taken after a review of your driving record or when the law requires it. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F16 | anchor: A01
After a suspension you pay the reinstatement fee plus the license application fee for your age group. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F17 | anchor: A01
Every conviction or bail forfeiture for a moving traffic violation adds points to your permanent driving record. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F18 | anchor: A01
If you build up 8 or more points within any 12-month period, you must attend Traffic Survival School, or your privilege may be suspended. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0062]

FACT_ID: sec19-F19 | anchor: A02
DUI, extreme DUI, aggravated DUI, reckless driving, racing on highways and aggressive driving each carry 8 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F20 | anchor: A02
Leaving the scene of a crash carries 6 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F21 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop for a signal or stop sign, or failing to yield the right-of-way, carries 6 points when it causes a death. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F22 | anchor: A02
Failing to stop for a signal or stop sign, or failing to yield the right-of-way, carries 4 points when it causes serious injury. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F23 | anchor: A02
A speeding violation carries 3 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F24 | anchor: A02
Driving over or parking in a gore area carries 3 points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F25 | anchor: A02
Wrong-way driving carries 2 points, the same as every other moving violation not listed separately. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F26 | anchor: A02
A conviction for running a red light or a flashing red light makes TSS mandatory on top of all court fines and fees. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F27 | anchor: A02
MVD may suspend or revoke your privilege, or require TSS, if you are convicted of frequent serious traffic offenses that show disregard for the safety of others. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F28 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of reckless driving or are a repeat reckless or negligent driver. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F29 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against your license if you commit or allow an unlawful or fraudulent use of your driver license. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F30 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of driving under the influence of alcohol, drugs or toxic vapors. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F31 | anchor: A02
Refusing or failing to complete a chemical test for alcohol or drug content brings a 12-month suspension, or 2 years for a second or later refusal within a 7-year period. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F32 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against your license if you have an unresolved judgment from another state. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F33 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against your license if you commit an offense that requires mandatory revocation upon conviction. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F34 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against the license of a driver under 21 who is convicted of receiving, drinking or possessing alcohol. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F35 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against the license of a driver under 21 who is convicted of any illegal drug violation. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F36 | anchor: A02
MVD may act against your license if you are medically unsafe to drive. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0063]

FACT_ID: sec19-F37 | anchor: A03
MVD may act against your license if, as a driver, you are convicted in a crash that caused death, personal injury or serious property damage. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F38 | anchor: A03
MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of violating a restriction on your license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F39 | anchor: A03
MVD may act against your license if you fail to comply with a certified ignition interlock device order. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F40 | anchor: A03
MVD may act against the license of a driver under 18 who is convicted of a first moving civil traffic violation or certain criminal traffic offenses. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F41 | anchor: A03
MVD may act against your license if you are convicted of wrong-way driving on a controlled-access highway. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F42 | anchor: A03
After a suspension or revocation period, you must pay the application fee to reinstate, and you may face an investigation and have to file an SR-22 Certificate of Insurance. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F43 | anchor: A03
If you are cited for driving on a suspended or revoked license, police may impound your vehicle for up to 30 days. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F44 | anchor: A03
A person convicted of driving on a suspended or revoked license may be eligible for a restricted driver license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F45 | anchor: A03
A first conviction for lacking or failing to show proof of current financial responsibility in the vehicle suspends the license, registration and plates for 3 months. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F46 | anchor: A03
A second financial responsibility violation within 36 months brings a 6-month suspension of the license, registration and plates. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F47 | anchor: A03
A third or later financial responsibility violation within 36 months brings a 1-year suspension of the license, registration and plates. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F48 | anchor: A03
Your license will be suspended if MVD is told that you missed a court appearance or did not pay a criminal traffic violation charge. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F49 | anchor: A03
Signing a traffic citation is your promise to appear in traffic court. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F50 | anchor: A03
A driver under 18 may have the privilege suspended for missing court, not paying a fine or not following any court order. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F51 | anchor: A03
Courts report people who are behind on traffic or boating fines, or who missed a criminal traffic or boating case, and MVD must then block renewal of any vehicle registration they own. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

FACT_ID: sec19-F52 | anchor: A03
A person under 18 may not use false identification to get someone to sell, serve, give or furnish a nitrous oxide container. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0064]

Misconceptions: revocation and suspension are different, since suspension is temporary while revocation removes the privilege until an investigation clears you; points stay on your permanent record, and it is eight points inside any twelve-month window that triggers Traffic Survival School; a red-light conviction brings mandatory school in addition to the court fine, not instead of it; refusing a chemical test is penalized on its own.
Mnemonics: Eight for the big six offenses, six for leaving a crash, three for speeding, two for the rest; insurance violations climb from three months to six months to a year.
Glossary: impound means towing and holding a vehicle, while immobilize means locking it in place; gore area means the space between a through roadway and an entrance or exit ramp, as the manual's freeway pages define it; chemical test means a test for alcohol or drug content; financial responsibility means proof of required vehicle insurance; restricted license means a license limited to certain driving.
Dynamic facts: point values, suspension lengths, impound periods and the grounds for MVD action are set by statute and MVD rules and can be amended.
